minutes.headline: Water commissioners approved a pilot-study contract for the Hickory Hills well, a GMC truck bid and a PFAS litigation signing.
minutes.summary: Landowner groups read a letter of conditions on reopening the Hickory Hills well, including lake levels, road damage and discharge, and the exchange turned heated. The board then voted to approve the engineering pilot-study agreement, sign onto PFAS litigation, and award the new truck bid. A Pond View Estates owner asked about water service outside the district, and the board agreed to seek counsel's opinion and to discuss the landowner letter in executive session after January 4th.

public_comment.topic: Read a letter of four conditions for supporting the Hickory Hills well: discharge plan, Woodlands road mitigation, 48-hour pump test discharged outside the watershed, and binding lake-level protections.
Clarified lake-level benchmarks (summer top of boards, winter drawdown) in response to board questions.
A Woodlands resident-side speaker argued about road pavement condition and responsibility for road damage from heavy trucks.
Asked about drawdown levels and said the lake community would absorb added weed-treatment costs.
Asked whether counsel had answered about a meter pit, holding tank and well outside the district to serve his development.

votes.motion: Superintendent to sign the agreement with the engineering firm for the pilot study portion, pending district counsel review
Authorize the superintendent to sign the aqueous film forming foam PFAS litigation document
Award the bid for the new GMC truck to Durant with aluminum utility body, downsizing to a lighter truck if it saves the stated amount

budget_items.what_was_said: Discussion of costs of pumping test with discharge pipe versus pilot study approach.
Motion to sign the agreement for the engineering firm's portion of the pilot study; the remaining portion goes to the contractor doing physical work.
Comparison of two bids, with the plow frame being priced by only one bidder; aluminum body is an upcharge and a trade-in is included.

budget_items.what_was_said: Superintendent speculated settlement could pay treatment and long-term maintenance costs, possibly lump sum or yearly.
Board hesitant about spending on another hydrogeologist review given costs already incurred.
A commissioner noted the landowners' proposal would require spending on a pipe to discharge outside the watershed.

decisions.decision: Board will review the landowners' letter with the superintendent and counsel and get back to them with a meeting date.
Superintendent to email district counsel the meter pit and holding tank questions for the Pond View Estates owner.
Next meeting moved to January 4th instead of December 28th.
Board will post counsel's letter and the pumpage-rate data with explanatory lake volume math.
Plan to discuss the landowners' letter in executive session after the January 4th regular meeting.

what_happened.line: The board voted by voice to have the superintendent sign the engineering firm's pilot-study agreement for the Hickory Hills well, pending district counsel review.
The board voted to authorize the superintendent to sign onto the aqueous film forming foam PFAS litigation.
The board voted to award the new GMC truck bid to Durant, with a lighter truck if it saves the stated amount.
Landowner groups read a letter of four conditions for supporting the Hickory Hills well; the board will review it with the superintendent and counsel and propose a meeting date.
The next meeting moved to January 4th, and the board plans to discuss the landowners' letter in executive session after it.

why_it_matters: Reopening the Hickory Hills well touches water supply and rates for district customers, and the pilot study and any discharge pipe are costs the district would carry.
The PFAS litigation signing could bring a settlement toward treatment and long-term maintenance costs, but the minutes show no outcome yet, so no effect on water bills can be assumed.

Counsel's opinion on water service outside the district, and the board's planned posting of counsel's letter and pumpage-rate data.
